cards.informal: For symmetric $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$: $A\succ0$ iff all nonempty leading principal minors are positive, equivalently all trailing ones; $A\succeq0$ iff all principal minors are nonnegative. If the first $n-1$ leading minors are positive and $\det A\ge0$, then $A\succeq0$. Writing $p_A(t)=\sum_j c_jt^j$, positive semidefiniteness is also equivalent to $(-1)^k c_{n-k}\ge0$ for every $0\le k\le n$, with zero coefficients retaining their degrees.
cards.conclusion: PD iff positive leading or trailing minors; PSD iff all principal minors are nonnegative, or iff $(-1)^k p_A.\operatorname{coeff}(n-k)\ge0$ for every $k\le n$; the positive-proper-leading-minors boundary criterion

cards.informal: Let $A=H+iK$ with $H,K$ Hermitian. If $H\succeq0$ then $\ker A\subseteq\ker H$, $\operatorname{rank}H\le\operatorname{rank}A$, and $A$ has the row/column inclusion property when the ranks agree (always when $H\succ0$). If $H\succ0$: $\det H\le|\det A|$ (Ostrowski–Taussky, equality iff $K=0$), $\det H+|\det K|\le|\det A|$ for $n\ge2$, and $(\det H)^{2/n}+|\det K|^{2/n}\le|\det A|^{2/n}$ (Fan).
cards.conclusion: null-space/rank relations; determinant lower bounds for $|\det A|$
cards.review_note: The actual PSD Hermitian part gives common kernels of A, its adjoint and its Hermitian real/imaginary parts, rank inequalities and row/column inclusion; the PD case has invertible principal submatrices. Exact relative diagonal determinant factors prove Ostrowski-Taussky and equality iff imaginary part zero, the determinant-sum inequality in dimension>=2, and the Fan 2/n power inequality in positive dimension.

clauses.statement: For positive semidefinite Hermitian part, the matrix kernel equals its adjoint kernel and the common kernel of its real and imaginary Hermitian parts; the Hermitian-part rank is no greater than the full rank, including empty dimension.

Equality of matrix and positive-semidefinite Hermitian-part ranks implies identical kernels and complex leading row and column inclusion. Positive definite Hermitian part makes every embedded principal submatrix invertible and gives both inclusion properties.

A positive definite Hermitian part and arbitrary Hermitian imaginary part admit exact relative-diagonal determinant products. Ostrowski-Taussky gives det(H)<=|det(H+iK)| with equality exactly when K=0, including dimension zero.
For dimension at least two, det(H)+|det(K)|<=|det(H+iK)|; for positive dimension, the sharp Fan exponent 2/n gives det(H)^(2/n)+|det(K)|^(2/n)<=|det(H+iK)|^(2/n), including singular K.

reviewed_clauses.statement: For positive semidefinite Hermitian part, the matrix kernel equals its adjoint kernel and the common kernel of its real and imaginary Hermitian parts; the Hermitian-part rank is no greater than the full rank, including empty dimension.

Equality of matrix and positive-semidefinite Hermitian-part ranks implies identical kernels and complex leading row and column inclusion. Positive definite Hermitian part makes every embedded principal submatrix invertible and gives both inclusion properties.

A positive definite Hermitian part and arbitrary Hermitian imaginary part admit exact relative-diagonal determinant products. Ostrowski-Taussky gives det(H)<=|det(H+iK)| with equality exactly when K=0, including dimension zero.
For dimension at least two, det(H)+|det(K)|<=|det(H+iK)|; for positive dimension, the sharp Fan exponent 2/n gives det(H)^(2/n)+|det(K)|^(2/n)<=|det(H+iK)|^(2/n), including singular K.

cards.informal: If $\hat A$ is obtained from $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ by deleting one row or one column, then with $q=\min(m,n)$ and $\hat\sigma_q:=0$ when the deletion lowers the smaller dimension: $\sigma_1(A)\ge\hat\sigma_1\ge\sigma_2(A)\ge\hat\sigma_2\ge\dots\ge\sigma_q(A)\ge\hat\sigma_q$. Iterating: for a $p\times r$ submatrix $A_{IJ}$, $\sigma_{i+(m-p)+(n-r)}(A)\le\sigma_i(A_{IJ})\le\sigma_i(A)$.
hypotheses: $\hat A$: one row or column deleted (or a general submatrix)
cards.conclusion: interlacing of $\sigma(A)$ and $\sigma(\hat A)$

cards.informal: Every real $m\times n$ matrix with $m\ge n$ has $A=UQ$, $Q=(A^\top A)^{1/2}\succeq0$ and $U^\top U=I_n$, at arbitrary rank. The positive factor is unique; the polar isometry is unique iff $\operatorname{rank}A=n$, when $U=A(A^\top A)^{-1/2}$. For $m\le n$, $A=PU$ with $P=(AA^\top)^{1/2}$ and a coisometry $UU^\top=I_m$, unique iff $\operatorname{rank}A=m$. In the square case one orthogonal $U$ gives $A=PU=UQ$. Every tall polar isometry and every wide polar coisometry is a nearest such factor to $A$ in every orthogonally invariant norm on its real matrix space.
hypotheses: $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$; $m\ge n$ for the isometry version and $m\le n$ for the coisometry version
cards.conclusion: tall $A=U(A^\top A)^{1/2}$ with $U^\top U=I_n$, wide $A=(AA^\top)^{1/2}U$ with $UU^\top=I_m$, exact full-rank uniqueness conditions and nearest factors in every invariant norm
cards.review_note: Isometry/coisometry dimensions and full-column/full-row-rank uniqueness are distinct. Rank-deficient polar factors still attain nearest-factor guarantees.

Equality $\|A-B\|_F^2=\sum_i(\sigma_i(A)-\sigma_i(B))^2$ holds iff $\operatorname{tr}AB^\top=\sum\sigma_i(A)\sigma_i(B)$, and then $AB^\top,B^\top A\succeq0$. In dimension zero the attained minimum for scaled orthogonal approximation is zero, with no division by the dimension.
hypotheses: $n>0$ for the normalized scalar $\operatorname{tr}(P)/n$; the empty-dimensional minimum is stated separately.
cards.conclusion: closed-form minima and minimisers of the Procrustes problems; equality case of von Neumann/Mirsky

cards.informal: Let $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric positive definite with extreme eigenvalues $\lambda_{\min},\lambda_{\max}$ and $\kappa=\lambda_{\max}/\lambda_{\min}$. Kantorovich: $(x^\top Ax)(x^\top A^{-1}x)\le\frac{(\lambda_{\min}+\lambda_{\max})^2}{4\lambda_{\min}\lambda_{\max}}\|x\|^4=\tfrac14(\kappa^{1/2}+\kappa^{-1/2})^2\|x\|^4$. Wielandt: for orthogonal $x,y$, $(x^\top Ay)^2\le\big(\frac{\lambda_{\max}-\lambda_{\min}}{\lambda_{\max}+\lambda_{\min}}\big)^2(x^\top Ax)(y^\top Ay)$. The two inequalities are equivalent.

cards.informal: For PSD $A,B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$: if $A\succ0$ and $B$ has positive diagonal then $A\circ B\succ0$; Hadamard powers $A^{\circ k}$ and $[f(a_{ij})]$ for $f$ with nonnegative Taylor coefficients (radius $>\max|a_{ij}|$) are PSD, $[e^{a_{ij}}]\succeq0$ (PD iff no two rows of $A$ coincide); Oppenheim: $\det(A\circ B)\ge\max\{\det A\prod b_{ii},\det B\prod a_{ii}\}$; for $A,B\succ0$: $A^{-1}\circ B^{-1}\succeq(A\circ B)^{-1}$, $A\circ A^{-1}\succeq I$, and, in positive dimension, $\lambda_{\min}(A\circ B)\ge\max\{\lambda_{\min}(AB),\lambda_{\min}(AB^\top)\}$; For real symmetric comparands, Hadamard products preserve the dominance $x^*Ax\ge|x^*Bx|$.
hypotheses: real symmetric comparands for the absolute quadratic dominance clause
cards.conclusion: the listed Loewner, determinant and eigenvalue inequalities for $A\circ B$
cards.review_note: Minimum-eigenvalue clause explicitly takes positive dimension. Absolute quadratic dominance is limited to real symmetric comparands, matching its known complex obstruction.

cards.informal: Let $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric positive definite and $B$ symmetric. Then $aA\preceq B\preceq bA$ iff every eigenvalue of $A^{-1}B$ lies in $[a,b]$; for $B\succeq0$, $A\succeq B$ iff $\rho(A^{-1}B)\le1$ iff $B=A^{1/2}XA^{1/2}$ with $0\preceq X\preceq I$, and $A^2\succeq B^2$ iff $\|A^{-1}B\|\le1$. If $A\succeq B\succeq0$: $\det A\ge\det B$, $\operatorname{tr}A\ge\operatorname{tr}B$ with equality iff $A=B$, $\lambda_i(A)\ge\lambda_i(B)$, and $B^{-1}\succeq A^{-1}$, $A^{1/2}\succeq B^{1/2}$ when defined.
cards.conclusion: equivalence of the Loewner sandwich with the relative spectrum; monotonicity of det, trace, eigenvalues, inverse and square root

cards.informal: For $X\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}$: $\begin{bmatrix}I&X\\X^\top&I\end{bmatrix}\succeq0$ ($\succ0$) iff $\|X\|\le1$ ($<1$). For $H=\begin{bmatrix}A&B\\B^\top&C\end{bmatrix}$ with $A,C\succeq0$, TFAE: $H\succeq0$; $(x^\top Ax)(y^\top Cy)\ge(x^\top By)^2$ for all $x,y$; $x^\top Ax+y^\top Cy\ge2|x^\top By|$; $B=A^{1/2}XC^{1/2}$ with $\|X\|\le1$; if $A,C\succ0$ also $\rho(B^\top A^{-1}BC^{-1})\le1$ (strict versions characterise $H\succ0$, equivalently $A\succ0$ and $C-B^\top A^{-1}B\succ0$). For $A,B\succeq0$: $A\succeq B$ iff $\begin{bmatrix}A&B\\B&A\end{bmatrix}\succeq0$. For $H\succ0$ and an index set $\alpha$: $(H^{-1})_{\alpha\alpha}\succeq(H_{\alpha\alpha})^{-1}$; $\begin{bmatrix}A&X\\X^\top&X^\top A^{-1}X\end{bmatrix}\succeq0$ for $A\succ0$.
cards.conclusion: the listed equivalences and Loewner inequalities
cards.review_note: Strict inequalities require positive definite diagonal blocks; non-strict square-root contraction factorization includes singular blocks.

baseline_audit.informal: For $X\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}$: $\begin{bmatrix}I&X\\X^\top&I\end{bmatrix}\succeq0$ ($\succ0$) iff $\|X\|\le1$ ($<1$). For $H=\begin{bmatrix}A&B\\B^\top&C\end{bmatrix}$ with $A,C\succeq0$, TFAE: $H\succeq0$; $(x^\top Ax)(y^\top Cy)\ge(x^\top By)^2$ for all $x,y$; $x^\top Ax+y^\top Cy\ge2|x^\top By|$; $B=A^{1/2}XC^{1/2}$ with $\|X\|\le1$; if $A,C\succ0$ also $\rho(B^\top A^{-1}BC^{-1})\le1$ (strict versions characterise $H\succ0$, equivalently $A\succ0$ and $C-B^\top A^{-1}B\succ0$). For $A,B\succeq0$: $A\succeq B$ iff $\begin{bmatrix}A&B\\B&A\end{bmatrix}\succeq0$. For $H\succ0$ and an index set $\alpha$: $(H^{-1})_{\alpha\alpha}\succeq(H_{\alpha\alpha})^{-1}$; $\begin{bmatrix}A&X\\X^\top&X^\top A^{-1}X\end{bmatrix}\succeq0$ for $A\succ0$.
baseline_audit.conclusion: the listed equivalences and Loewner inequalities

cards.informal: For symmetric positive definite $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$: $\det A\le\prod_ia_{ii}$ with equality iff $A$ is diagonal for positive definite $A$; for PSD $A$, equality holds iff $A$ is diagonal or some diagonal entry is zero (Hadamard), hence $|\det B|\le\prod_j\|b_j\|_2$ for any square $B$ with columns $b_j$ (equality iff orthogonal columns or a zero column); $\det\begin{bmatrix}A_{11}&A_{12}\\A_{21}&A_{22}\end{bmatrix}\le\det A_{11}\det A_{22}$ (Fischer); $\det A_{\alpha\cup\beta}\det A_{\alpha\cap\beta}\le\det A_\alpha\det A_\beta$ (Koteljanskiĭ); and the normalised products $P_k^{1/\binom{n-1}{k-1}}$ of $k\times k$ principal minors decrease in $k$ (Szász).

baseline_audit.informal: For symmetric positive definite $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$: $\det A\le\prod_ia_{ii}$ with equality iff $A$ is diagonal for positive definite $A$; for PSD $A$, equality holds iff $A$ is diagonal or some diagonal entry is zero (Hadamard), hence $|\det B|\le\prod_j\|b_j\|_2$ for any square $B$ with columns $b_j$ (equality iff orthogonal columns or a zero column); $\det\begin{bmatrix}A_{11}&A_{12}\\A_{21}&A_{22}\end{bmatrix}\le\det A_{11}\det A_{22}$ (Fischer); $\det A_{\alpha\cup\beta}\det A_{\alpha\cap\beta}\le\det A_\alpha\det A_\beta$ (Koteljanskiĭ); and the normalised products $P_k^{1/\binom{n-1}{k-1}}$ of $k\times k$ principal minors decrease in $k$ (Szász).
hypotheses: $A=A^\top\succ0$; determinant inequalities also hold for PSD input, with equality cases qualified separately.
baseline_audit.conclusion: the listed determinant inequalities with equality cases
baseline_audit.review_note: Semidefinite Hadamard equality correctly includes a zero diagonal entry. Positive-dimensional Szász exponents and principal minor endpoint restrictions must be respected.

current_atlas_snapshot.informal: For symmetric positive definite $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$: $\det A\le\prod_ia_{ii}$ with equality iff $A$ is diagonal for positive definite $A$; for PSD $A$, equality holds iff $A$ is diagonal or some diagonal entry is zero (Hadamard), hence $|\det B|\le\prod_j\|b_j\|_2$ for any square $B$ with columns $b_j$ (equality iff orthogonal columns or a zero column); $\det\begin{bmatrix}A_{11}&A_{12}\\A_{21}&A_{22}\end{bmatrix}\le\det A_{11}\det A_{22}$ (Fischer); $\det A_{\alpha\cup\beta}\det A_{\alpha\cap\beta}\le\det A_\alpha\det A_\beta$ (Koteljanskiĭ); and the normalised products $P_k^{1/\binom{n-1}{k-1}}$ of $k\times k$ principal minors decrease in $k$ (Szász).
hypotheses: $A=A^\top\succ0$; determinant inequalities also hold for PSD input, with equality cases qualified separately.
current_atlas_snapshot.conclusion: the listed determinant inequalities with equality cases

cards.readback: Semidefinite Hadamard equality correctly includes a zero diagonal entry. Positive-dimensional Szász exponents and principal minor endpoint restrictions must be respected.
